newsitem.title: USA: Maine leaders pledge tax break for Bath Iron Works.
newsitem.headline: Maine leaders pledge tax break for Bath Iron Works.

text.p: Maine Gov. Angus King Monday promosed support for additional tax breaks to aid an expansion and modernization of the Bath Iron Works unit (BIW) of General Dynamics .

King's called for granting the warship builder $60 million in rebates of state payroll taxes over the next 20 years. BIW is already slated to receive a $53 million break through a repeal of the tax on manufacturing equipment.
Bath officials had already approved $81 million in local property tax abatements over the next 20 yeas.
King acknowledged that the $3.7 billion two-year budget approved by lawmakers in March did not include money to reduce BIW's payroll taxes. The rebate will have to be approved by the legislature.

BIW, the state's largest private employer with 7,300 workers, has proposed a nearly $600 million facility overhaul that includes building a new drydock and "building ways" used to constuct and launch ships.
The company, which is dependent on U.S. Navy contracts, has said it needs to overhaul the shipyard if it is to compete for future warship contracts with Mississippi-based Ingalls Shipbuilding.

King said the payroll tax rebate is contingent on BIW maintaining at least 3,500 employees, but BIW president Allan Cameron said BIW could not pledge keep its current employement level once the modernization is completed.
